label: Heat, low temperature (< 150 degC)
covers: Heat supplied to a process from a site heat system at a delivery temperature below 150 degC: hot water and low-pressure steam for washing and CIP, pasteurizing, bleaching, stock heating, evaporation, low-temperature drying; generic low-temperature direct heaters. Banded on the temperature the process needs, not on the steam grade. Cogeneration sits here too: a CHP unit is a technology that supplies this band, with electricity as a co-product (2026-09-14, reversing the separate chp end use).
steam: LP steam and hot water. Boilers in food and paper raise 121-177 degC steam for these duties [NREL97 boiler/steam rows, SIC 20xx, 26xx]. Share of steam-served heat below 150 degC: food 99%, pulp and paper 81%, chemicals 80%, non-ferrous 100%, refining 32% [NREL118].
draws-on: none (is a source)
energy-inputs: natural gas, biomass, black liquor, by-product gases, electricity (electric boilers, heat pumps), solar thermal, recovered heat; CHP prime movers (gas turbines, engines, back-pressure turbines)
note: 150 degC is roughly where commercial heat pumps stop [design doc s2; etsap_2013_002 165 degC; rtc_2023_001 heat pump < 160 degC], so this is the band where they compete. caelp_2024_001 puts 84% of food and 80% of pulp and paper indirect heat below 100 degC but only 28% of chemicals.
sources: design doc s2; NREL118; NREL97; etsap_2013_002 p.2, p.8 (heat pump 165 degC); rtc_2023_001 p.13 (heat pump < 160 degC); caelp_2024_001 p.11, p.36

label: Heat, medium temperature (150-400 degC)
covers: Heat supplied at 150-400 degC: medium- and high-pressure steam, thermal oil and direct heaters for distillation reboilers, digesters, stripping, polymer melting and extrusion, panel pressing, and fired heaters feeding refinery distillation. Cogeneration sits here too, as a technology supplying the band rather than an end use of its own (2026-09-14).
steam: MP/HP steam. Share of steam-served heat at 150-400 degC: iron and steel 100% (assigned 177 degC), refining 68% (49% at 200-250 degC), other industry 74%, pulp and paper 19%, chemicals 17% [NREL118]. CHP process steam 50-150 psig, 298-380 degF (148-193 degC) [epa_2017_001]. CIMS Mining.Steam carries 900 psig boilers and cogen.
draws-on: none (is a source)
energy-inputs: natural gas, refinery fuel gas, oil, biomass, electricity (electric boilers, resistance heaters), thermal storage; CHP prime movers (gas turbines, engines, back-pressure turbines)
note: Heat pumps fall away above about 200 degC [caelp_2024_001 p.11 uses 200 degC as the practical delivery bound], leaving combustion, electric boilers and heaters, thermal storage and CHP.
sources: design doc s2; NREL118; epa_2017_001; caelp_2024_001 p.11; nrcan_2025_001

label: Heat, high temperature (> 400 degC)
covers: Heat above 400 degC supplied by a fired heater or furnace that is separable from the unit doing the transformation: refinery process heaters for conversion units, generic industrial furnaces and heaters, superheated steam above 400 degC. Heat released INSIDE a sector's own process unit (kiln, blast furnace, cracker furnace, lime kiln, glass furnace) is not here; it belongs to that sector's end use.
steam: Rare as a process demand: 2% of chemicals steam-served heat and 4% in basic chemicals is above 400 degC; none elsewhere [NREL118].
draws-on: none (is a source)
energy-inputs: natural gas, refinery fuel gas, oil, hydrogen, electricity (resistance, induction, plasma)
note: NRCan records refinery furnaces at 200-700 degC (79 PJ), straddling medium and high; its bands are < 200 / 200-700 / > 700 degC and do not map onto ours.

label: On-site power-only generation
covers: Electricity generated on site with no useful heat recovered: diesel and gas gensets at off-grid mines and oil-and-gas sites, gas turbines and engines, condensing steam turbines, power plants firing by-product gases, and solar, wind and storage in site microgrids.
steam: None; condensing steam turbines raise steam but deliver no process heat.
draws-on: none
energy-inputs: diesel, natural gas, by-product gases, solar, wind, batteries
note: Brought into scope on the user's decision (2026-09-11), reversing design doc s1, which put power-only generation out of scope. At isolated northern mines diesel is over 80% of energy use (Energies 2026 review). The CHP/power-only boundary is heat recovery.

label: Pumps
covers: Motor-, engine- and turbine-driven pumps moving liquids and slurries around a site. Excludes pipeline pumping, which is an oil-and-gas end use.
draws-on: none
energy-inputs: electricity; natural gas or steam where the driver is a direct drive
note: The DOE Manufacturing Energy and Carbon Footprints (2018 MECS series, built on EIA MECS) split machine drive into pumps, fans, compressed air, materials handling, materials processing and other systems; MECS itself reports machine drive only as a total. These five end uses follow the footprint split, and its 'other systems' residual is not carried - motor-driven equipment none of the five covers is filed under materials processing.

label: Fans and blowers
covers: Process fans, blowers and induced- and forced-draught sets. Excludes building ventilation and mine ventilation, which are their own end uses.
draws-on: none
energy-inputs: electricity; natural gas or steam where the driver is a direct drive
note: The DOE Manufacturing Energy and Carbon Footprints (2018 MECS series, built on EIA MECS) split machine drive into pumps, fans, compressed air, materials handling, materials processing and other systems; MECS itself reports machine drive only as a total. These five end uses follow the footprint split, and its 'other systems' residual is not carried - motor-driven equipment none of the five covers is filed under materials processing.

label: Compressed air
covers: Compressed-air systems and the process compression that serves them. Excludes pipeline and gas-processing compression, which are oil-and-gas end uses.
draws-on: none (waste heat is recoverable to heat-low-temp)
energy-inputs: electricity; natural gas or steam where the driver is a direct drive
note: The DOE Manufacturing Energy and Carbon Footprints (2018 MECS series, built on EIA MECS) split machine drive into pumps, fans, compressed air, materials handling, materials processing and other systems; MECS itself reports machine drive only as a total. These five end uses follow the footprint split, and its 'other systems' residual is not carried - motor-driven equipment none of the five covers is filed under materials processing.

label: Materials handling
covers: Conveyors, cranes, hoists, stackers and reclaimers moving solids around a site.
draws-on: none
energy-inputs: electricity; natural gas or steam where the driver is a direct drive
note: The DOE Manufacturing Energy and Carbon Footprints (2018 MECS series, built on EIA MECS) split machine drive into pumps, fans, compressed air, materials handling, materials processing and other systems; MECS itself reports machine drive only as a total. These five end uses follow the footprint split, and its 'other systems' residual is not carried - motor-driven equipment none of the five covers is filed under materials processing.

label: Materials processing
covers: Motor-driven size reduction, mixing, forming and separation that is NOT already counted in a sector end use - comminution, mechanical pulping, rolling and cement grinding all stay with their sector.
draws-on: none
energy-inputs: electricity; natural gas or steam where the driver is a direct drive
note: The DOE Manufacturing Energy and Carbon Footprints (2018 MECS series, built on EIA MECS) split machine drive into pumps, fans, compressed air, materials handling, materials processing and other systems; MECS itself reports machine drive only as a total. These five end uses follow the footprint split, and its 'other systems' residual is not carried - motor-driven equipment none of the five covers is filed under materials processing.

label: HVAC heating
covers: Heating and ventilating plant buildings and warehouses: unit heaters, radiant tubes, make-up air units, supply and exhaust air handling, heat-recovery ventilation and building heat pumps.
heat-process-temp: < 150; site steam 121 (160-177 at a few SICs) [NREL97]
steam: Space heat is often taken from site steam; boiler space-heat duty 121 degC [NREL97].
draws-on: integral (fired and electric unit heaters); heat-low-temp (site steam)
energy-inputs: natural gas, propane, oil, electricity
note: Mine ventilation and mine air heating are a mining end use. Building ventilation was folded into space heating and space cooling on 2026-09-16. Renamed from space-heating (naming and end-use split 2026-10-23 (modeller)): commercial-scale building HVAC; residential comes later.

label: HVAC cooling
covers: Cooling and ventilating offices, control rooms and production space, including supply and exhaust air handling.
draws-on: none
energy-inputs: electricity
note: Building ventilation was folded into space heating and space cooling on 2026-09-16. Renamed from space-cooling (naming and end-use split 2026-10-23 (modeller)); every sector's hvac cooling node.

label: Lighting
covers: Interior and yard lighting, and its controls.
draws-on: none
energy-inputs: electricity
note: Service unit lumen-hours (Mlm-h), ruling 2026-10-14; the CIMS lighting nodes are to move from GJ to lumens and split into general and high-bay lighting (cims/hierarchy-change-requests.md).

label: On-site mobile equipment
covers: Non-road vehicles and equipment used on site: construction equipment, loaders, forklifts, yard trucks, slag and log handling, oil-and-gas field vehicles.
draws-on: none
energy-inputs: diesel, propane, electricity (battery)
note: Material because construction sits in other-industry: construction is 3.1% of Canadian industrial energy, mostly off-road diesel (NRCan Trends 2017). NRCan also shows 1.3 PJ diesel in pulp and paper. Mine haulage and oil-sands truck fleets stay with their own sector end uses.
sources: nrcan_2025_001; NRCan Energy Use in Canada: Trends 2017 (web); CIMS

label: CO2 capture, concentrated streams
covers: Capture from process streams where the CO2 is already concentrated and nitrogen-free: shifted syngas and acid-gas removal in ammonia, methanol and hydrogen plants (including upgrader hydrogen units), formation CO2 removed at gas-processing plants, fermentation CO2 at ethanol plants, pre-combustion capture on gasifiers, oxygen-blown iron routes (HIsarna, smelting reduction, syngas DRI, top-gas recycling), indirectly heated calciners, oxy-fuel flue gas. The work is drying and compression, with little or no solvent regeneration.
draws-on: compressed-air (dehydration and compression)
energy-inputs: electricity (compression, dehydration)
note: IPCC Table 11.3: 99% reduction, TRL 9, <= USD40/t, available today; footnote f calls disposal of concentrated CO2 at USD15-40/t well established. IPCC names HIsarna and syngas DRI as concentrated; smelting reduction, Corex and top-gas recycling are put here by analogy (oxygen-blown, nitrogen-free gas) and need a source. An SMR has both kinds: process CO2 from the shift is concentrated, the reformer furnace flue is dilute. CIMS books one rate for it. Integrated routes (hisarna-ccs, shaft-furnace_syngas_ccs, calciner_ccs) stay on their sector end use as technology choices; this end use is the capture service they draw on. CIMS has no capture option on ethanol fermentation CO2; its Ethanol.CCS serves only boilers. Sector and cross-sector rows named `<host>_ccs-concentrated` point here: the capture plant's cost and energy are held on this end use once and are not repeated on the host row, which carries only the host-side effects.

label: CO2 capture, diffuse (dilute) streams
covers: Post-combustion capture from flue gas where the CO2 is diluted in nitrogen: boilers, CHP, fired heaters, cement and lime kiln stacks, cracker furnaces, FCC regenerators, sinter strands and EAF off-gas.
heat-process-temp: regeneration temperature not in held sources
steam: Post-combustion reboiler duty 3,750 kJ/kg CO2 [UKERC CH-SC28 via johansson_2012_001]. CIMS asks 3.4-4.8 GJ natural gas per t CO2 for it (Petroleum Refining, Iron and Steel, Industrial Minerals .CCS).
draws-on: heat-low-temp (solvent regeneration); fans-and-blowers (flue-gas booster fans); compressed-air (CO2 compression)
energy-inputs: steam or natural gas (regeneration), electricity (fans, compression)
note: IPCC Table 11.3: up to 90% reduction, TRL 6-7, <= USD120/t, from 2025. For cement IPCC splits the same plant two ways: calcination CO2 from an indirect calciner <= USD40/t (concentrated), fuel CO2 <= USD120/t (dilute). Direct air capture is its own end use, direct-air-capture. IPCC's term is 'diluted in nitrogen'; 'diffuse' here means the same thing. Sector and cross-sector rows named `<host>_ccs-diffuse` point here: the capture plant's cost and energy are held on this end use once and are not repeated on the host row, which carries only the host-side effects, such as the steam drawn for regeneration.

label: Direct air capture
covers: Capture of CO2 from ambient air by liquid-solvent or solid-sorbent processes, with compression; the CO2 goes to storage (carbon removal) or becomes a carbon feedstock for synthetic fuels and chemicals.
heat-process-tier: low-temp or high-temp (depends on the process)
steam: Not quantified in any held source. Liquid-solvent systems regenerate in a high-temperature calciner, solid-sorbent systems at low temperature, so the band is set by the technology, not the end use.
draws-on: heat-high-temp (liquid-solvent calciner); heat-low-temp (solid-sorbent regeneration); fans-and-blowers (air contactors)
energy-inputs: electricity (air contactors, compression), heat (natural gas, electricity, recovered heat)
note: IPCC Table 11.3: up to 99% reduction, TRL 3, about USD94-232/t, available by 2030, listed as a carbon source for CoOxHy fuels and feedstocks. Kept apart from point-source capture because it serves no emitting process: it draws CO2 from air rather than a stack, is sited independently of any plant, and competes as a removal or a feedstock supply rather than as abatement on a process. The harmonized row tp-1509 stores its abatement cost as 2.0 USD/t; the IPCC cell reads about USD94-232/t, so that is an extraction error.

label: CO2 transport and storage
covers: Pipeline transport of captured CO2 by provincial route and its injection into geological storage or EOR.
energy-inputs: electricity (compression, injection)
note: Each tonne needs both transport and storage: pipeline_co2 and well_co2-storage are complements here, not alternatives. Added 2026-09-25.

label: Cokemaking
covers: Coke ovens and the by-product plant.
heat-process-temp: coal heated to 1000-1100, flue gas 1150-1350 [etsap_2010_002 p.2]; coking 1427 [NREL97 SIC 3312]
steam: By-product plant steam at 177 degC [NREL97 SIC 3312 coking/steam].
draws-on: integral (ovens); heat-medium-temp (by-product plant)
energy-inputs: coking coal; coke-oven and blast-furnace gas for underfiring
note: NRCan: 16.9 PJ coke and coke-oven gas at > 700 degC.

label: Sintering and pelletizing
covers: Sinter plants and pellet induration at the steelworks.
draws-on: integral (sinter strand and induration furnace); fans-and-blowers (windboxes and cooler fans); materials-handling (feed and product)
energy-inputs: coke breeze, natural gas, oil, electricity
note: Most Canadian pellets are made at the mine; see mining pelletizing, which uses the same technologies.

label: Ironmaking
covers: Reduction of iron ore: blast furnace with hot stoves, direct reduction (shaft furnace with reformer or hydrogen), smelting reduction. The routes compete to supply the same service.
heat-process-temp: blast furnace 2200-2300 [rtc_2023_001 p.75]; plasma blast furnace flame 2150 [etsap_2010_002 p.4]
steam: Blast-furnace blowers and auxiliaries draw site steam, which NREL assigns 177 degC for iron and steel [NREL118] -> heat-medium-temp.
draws-on: integral (blast furnace and stoves, DRI shaft, smelter); fans-and-blowers (blast-furnace blowers); steel-oxygen-supply (enrichment); materials-handling (burden and product)
energy-inputs: coke and PCI coal as reductant and fuel; natural gas (DRI, injection); hydrogen (future DRI); electricity (plasma, electric smelting)
note: NRCan: blast furnaces 40.7 PJ; DRI methane reformer 14.4 PJ natural gas. CIMS does not split ironmaking from steelmaking.

label: Steelmaking
covers: BOF and EAF (scrap and DRI charge), ladle metallurgy and ladle preheating.
steam: Minor; none reported in held sources.
draws-on: integral (converter and arc); steel-oxygen-supply (BOF blowing and EAF lancing); fans-and-blowers (fume extraction)
energy-inputs: electricity (EAF); oxygen; chemical heat of hot metal; natural gas (ladle preheat, oxy-fuel burners); charge carbon
note: Scrap availability bounds the EAF share; the EAF/BOF split is a technology choice within this end use.

label: Oxygen supply
covers: Cryogenic and adsorption air separation supplying oxygen to the basic oxygen furnace, the electric arc furnace and the blast furnace, on site or over the fence.
draws-on: none (the air compressors are the process)
energy-inputs: electricity (compression)
note: Moved out of the cross-sector air-separation end use (2026-09-14): oxygen is a sector service, sized by the steel route. Small oxygen uses elsewhere - glass oxy-fuel firing, oxy-fuel capture, merchant industrial gases - are not carried as end uses.

label: Casting
covers: Ingot, continuous, thin-slab and strip casting of liquid steel into semis.
draws-on: integral (tundish and mould, and ingot soaking pits); pumps (mould and machine cooling water)
energy-inputs: electricity, water; natural gas and oil (ingot soaking pits)

label: Reheating
covers: Reheating slabs, billets and blooms to rolling temperature, and hot charging that avoids it.
draws-on: integral (reheating furnaces)
energy-inputs: natural gas, coke-oven and blast-furnace gas, oil, electricity (induction)
note: NRCan: high-temperature furnaces 45.9 PJ (natural gas, coal, coke-oven gas) at > 700 degC.

label: Hot and cold rolling
covers: Roughing and finishing stands, section, bar, rod and tube mills, tandem and reversing cold mills, acid pickling and skin pass.
heat-process-temp: pickling and rinse baths; pickling steam 160 [NREL97 SIC 3312]
steam: Pickling line steam at about 160 degC [NREL97 SIC 3312].
draws-on: heat-low-temp (pickling and cleaning baths); materials-processing (mill drives); pumps (roll cooling and hydraulics)
energy-inputs: electricity (mill drives, electrolytic cleaning), steam, acid
note: Rolling heat comes from reheating.

label: Annealing and coating
covers: Batch and continuous annealing, tempering, electrical-steel treatment, hot-dip galvanizing, electro-galvanizing and tin plating.
heat-process-temp: annealing 760 by fuel, 160 by steam [NREL97 SIC 3312]; molten zinc about 460
draws-on: integral (annealing and line furnaces, zinc pots)
energy-inputs: natural gas, oil, electricity; hydrogen or nitrogen atmosphere; zinc, tin
note: Zinc-bath temperature is not in held or checked sources.

label: Clinker production
covers: Raw meal preparation and drying, preheater and precalciner, rotary kiln, clinker cooler.
heat-process-temp: kiln 1400-1500 [etsap_2010_003]; raw materials ~250, calciner ~900, kiln ~1400 [rtc_2023_001 p.47]; calcining 1482 [NREL97 SIC 3241]
steam: None; NREL finds no steam use in cement [NREL118].
draws-on: integral (kiln, precalciner and cooler); fans-and-blowers (induced-draught, cooler and preheater fans); materials-handling (raw meal and clinker)
energy-inputs: coal, petroleum coke, natural gas, alternative fuels, electricity (raw mill, fans); process CO2 from calcination
note: NRCan: calciners 55.5 PJ at > 700 degC. Raw milling is kept here, not in machine drive, because it moves with the kiln choice.

label: Cement grinding
covers: Finish grinding, supplementary cementitious material preparation and blending, alternative binders.
draws-on: materials-processing (finish mills); materials-handling (clinker, additions and cement)
energy-inputs: electricity
note: Clinker ratio is decided here, which is why grinding is not folded into machine drive.

label: Lime and dolime calcination
covers: Lime and dolomitic lime kilns.
draws-on: integral (kiln); fans-and-blowers (combustion and cooling air)
energy-inputs: natural gas, coal, petroleum coke; process CO2
note: NRCan: lime calciners 10.7 PJ at > 700 degC.

label: Glass melting
covers: Batch and cullet preparation, melting and refining in container, flat, fibre and specialty glass furnaces; mineral wool melting.
heat-process-temp: glass melting 1538-1593, refining 816-1260 [NREL97 SIC 3211, 3221, 3229]; mineral wool melting 1593 [SIC 3296]
steam: Minor: mineral wool plant boilers at 160 degC [NREL97 SIC 3296].
draws-on: integral (glass furnaces); fans-and-blowers (combustion air); materials-handling (batch and cullet)
energy-inputs: natural gas, electricity (boosting, all-electric melters), oxygen
note: Split from melting-and-firing on 2026-09-16, following the CIMS hierarchy glass nodes: glass furnaces and ceramic kilns have different technology sets.

label: Glass forming and finishing
covers: Forming, annealing lehrs, tempering and fire polishing of glass products.
draws-on: integral (annealing lehrs and tempering furnaces); compressed-air (forming machines and quenching)
energy-inputs: natural gas, electricity
note: Split from melting-and-firing on 2026-09-16: annealing and tempering are a different energy service from melting.

label: Ceramic firing
covers: Brick, tile, sanitaryware and refractory firing in tunnel, roller and periodic kilns.
draws-on: integral (kilns); fans-and-blowers (combustion and cooling air)
energy-inputs: natural gas, electricity
note: Split from melting-and-firing on 2026-09-16.

label: Drying and low-temperature calcining
covers: Gypsum calcining to stucco, clay and brick drying, other mineral product drying.
heat-process-temp: gypsum calcining 171, drying 227 [NREL97 SIC 3275]; ceramic drying 316 [SIC 3251]
draws-on: integral (direct-fired dryers and calciners); fans-and-blowers (dryer air)
energy-inputs: natural gas

label: Olefins (high-value chemicals)
covers: Ethylene and propylene: ethane and naphtha steam crackers (Alberta and Sarnia), propane dehydrogenation (Alberta), and the alternative routes (methanol-to-olefins, ethanol dehydration, biomass, electric cracking).
steam: Stripping steam at 54-116 degC [NREL97 row 281331] -> heat-low-temp.
draws-on: integral (furnaces, and the cold-box refrigeration that is part of the process); heat-low-temp (separation); pumps (reflux and quench)
energy-inputs: ethane or naphtha feedstock; by-product fuel gas; natural gas; electricity (compressors, future e-cracker)
note: Renamed from steam-cracking (petrochemicals restructure 2026-10-23 (modeller: whatever makes most sense for Canada)).

label: Chlor-alkali and sodium chlorate
covers: Chlorine-caustic electrolysis, caustic evaporation, sodium chlorate cells.
steam: Evaporator steam at 104-121 degC [NREL97 SIC 2812] -> heat-low-temp.
draws-on: heat-low-temp (evaporators); pumps (brine and electrolyte)
energy-inputs: electricity (dominant), steam
note: Sodium chlorate supplies pulp bleaching, which is why it is material in Canada.

label: Nitric and adipic acid
covers: Ammonia oxidation to nitric acid, and adipic acid made by nitric acid oxidation: the N2O-emitting processes.
heat-process-temp: exothermic; ammonia oxidation temperature not in held sources
steam: Nitric acid plants are net steam exporters; not quantified in held sources.
draws-on: integral (ammonia burner, absorption train and oxidation reactors); none (a source: nitric acid plants export steam)
energy-inputs: ammonia (feedstock), electricity, steam (adipic acid)
note: Split from other-chemicals on 2026-09-16 under the emissions rule: N2O process emissions, abated by catalytic or thermal destruction. The CIMS hierarchy gained a nitric acid node on 2026-09-17.

label: Ethanol production
covers: Grain (corn, wheat) dry milling, liquefaction and cooking, fermentation, distillation and dehydration, stillage evaporation, distillers-grain drying; cellulosic ethanol.
heat-process-temp: steam-served heat p10/p50/p90 88/119/135 [NREL118 NAICS 325193]; direct heat 788-871 [NREL118], a value NREL assigns from SIC 2869 rather than measured for ethanol
steam: All of ethanol's steam-served heat is below 150 degC [NREL118 NAICS 325193], so it is heat-pump and MVR territory.
draws-on: heat-low-temp (cooking, distillation and evaporation); integral (grain dryers); pumps (mash and beer)
energy-inputs: natural gas, electricity, biomass; grain or cellulosic feedstock
note: Canada has about 1,900 million L/yr of ethanol nameplate capacity (CER). In the US, ethyl alcohol is 10% of chemical-sector energy (307 TBtu, DOE 2015). Fermentation CO2 is nearly pure: co2-capture-concentrated. CIMS's Ethanol.Agricultural Input (farm diesel for feedstock) is agriculture and stays out of scope.
sources: NREL118; CER bioenergy overview (web); DOE 2015 chemicals bandwidth study (web)

label: Biodiesel production
covers: Oil and fat pretreatment, transesterification, methanol recovery, glycerin refining, biodiesel distillation.
heat-process-temp: steam-served heat for NAICS 325199 as for 325193: p50 119 [NREL118], not biodiesel-specific
steam: Low-temperature steam for reaction and methanol recovery; no biodiesel-specific source held.
draws-on: heat-low-temp (transesterification and methanol recovery)
energy-inputs: natural gas, electricity, methanol; vegetable oil, tallow or used cooking oil feedstock
note: Canada has about 700 million L/yr of biodiesel capacity (CER). Renewable diesel (HVO) is a different product and route: see renewable-diesel-and-saf.

label: Renewable diesel and SAF
covers: Dedicated hydrotreating (HEFA/HVO) units, including converted refineries, that make renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel from vegetable oils, tallow and used cooking oil: feed pretreatment, hydrodeoxygenation, isomerization, fractionation.
heat-process-temp: as refinery hydroprocessing, reactors ~260-480 [rtc_2023_001 p.97]; not specific to renewable diesel
steam: Process and stripping steam, as in refinery hydrotreating.
draws-on: heat-medium-temp (fired heaters); heat-high-temp (fired heaters); centralized-hydrogen-production (hydrotreating hydrogen)
energy-inputs: hydrogen (large), natural gas, electricity; lipid feedstock
note: Moved from petroleum-refining on the user's decision (2026-09-11). Canada produced about 687 million L in 2024 and planned capacity could triple (CER). Its hydrogen demand is what separates its energy use from biodiesel's. Co-processing in existing refinery hydrotreaters stays in refining.

label: Renewable natural gas
covers: Biogas raised from anaerobic digestion or landfill and upgraded to pipeline specification, and biomass gasification to methane.
draws-on: heat-low-temp (digester heating); compressed-air (upgrading and injection compression)
energy-inputs: biomass, manure, municipal and landfill waste; electricity, low-temperature heat
note: Moved out of the cross-sector hydrogen-and-fuel-supply end use (2026-09-14): RNG is produced for sale into the gas system, which makes it a biofuels product rather than a site service.

label: Centralized hydrogen production
covers: Merchant hydrogen produced for sale rather than for an on-site process: steam methane and autothermal reformers with and without capture, gasification, and grid- or dedicated-renewable electrolysis at plant scale.
steam: Reformers raise HP steam as a by-product.
draws-on: integral (reformer firebox); compressed-air (product compression)
energy-inputs: natural gas, coal, petroleum coke, biomass, electricity
note: New sector, 2026-09-14. Split from on-site production because the plant is sized by the merchant market, not by one host process, and because its emissions and its capture economics are the hydrogen sector's, not the user's.

label: Hydrogen distribution
covers: Compression, pipeline transmission and distribution of hydrogen to industrial users, including booster compression, and liquefaction and trucking where there is no pipeline.
draws-on: none (the compression is the process)
energy-inputs: electricity (compression, liquefaction)
note: New sector, 2026-09-14. Distribution energy is a real cost of centralized supply and is what distinguishes it from production at the point of use.

label: Crude distillation
covers: Desalting, atmospheric and vacuum distillation.
steam: Stripping and ejector steam. Refinery steam-served heat 32% < 150 degC, 68% at 150-400 (49% at 200-250) [NREL118].
draws-on: heat-medium-temp (crude and vacuum heaters, stripping steam); pumps (crude charge and reflux); fans-and-blowers (air coolers)
energy-inputs: refinery fuel gas, natural gas, steam, electricity
note: The heaters are CIMS's separate Direct Heat service, hence 'draws' rather than 'integral'.

label: Conversion, upgrading and treating
covers: FCC, hydrocracking, coking, catalytic reforming, alkylation, isomerization, asphalt and lubes, hydrotreating and sulphur recovery. Co-processing bio-feedstock in an existing hydrotreater stays here as a feedstock choice; dedicated renewable diesel and SAF units are in biofuels.
steam: Stripping and MP steam (see crude distillation for the refinery-wide split).
draws-on: heat-medium-temp (process heaters); heat-high-temp (process heaters); integral (FCC regenerator); refinery-hydrogen (hydrotreating and hydrocracking)
energy-inputs: refinery fuel gas, natural gas, petroleum coke (FCC coke), hydrogen, electricity
note: NRCan: FCC catalyst regeneration burns 50.8 PJ of petroleum coke as captive combustion.

label: On-site hydrogen production
covers: Hydrogen made at the refinery for hydrotreating and hydrocracking: steam methane and autothermal reformers with and without capture, petroleum-coke gasification, and electrolysis.
steam: Reformer convection sections raise HP steam.
draws-on: integral (reformer firebox); compressed-air (make-up and recycle compression)
energy-inputs: natural gas, refinery fuel gas, petroleum coke, electricity
note: Moved out of the cross-sector hydrogen-and-fuel-supply end use (2026-09-14): a refinery hydrogen plant is sized and fuelled by the refinery. 37.6 PJ of reformer natural gas is booked as a non-energetic input.

label: Wood preparation
covers: Log thawing, debarking, chipping and chip screening for pulp mills.
steam: Winter log and chip thawing uses low-pressure steam or hot water; not quantified in held sources.
draws-on: heat-low-temp (log and chip thawing in winter); materials-handling (log and chip conveying)
energy-inputs: electricity, steam
note: Split out on 2026-09-16: debarking and chipping serve every virgin-fibre route, not only chemical pulping.

label: Chemical pulping and bleaching
covers: Kraft and semi-chemical digesting, washing, oxygen delignification and bleaching.
heat-process-temp: digesting 171 by steam [NREL97 SIC 2611]; chemical preparation 60-200, bleaching 60-150 [rtc_2023_001 p.88]
steam: Digester steam at 171 degC -> heat-medium-temp; bleaching and washing -> heat-low-temp [NREL97; rtc_2023_001 p.88].
draws-on: heat-medium-temp (digester); heat-low-temp (washing and bleaching); pumps (stock and liquor)
energy-inputs: steam, electricity, bleaching chemicals

label: Mechanical pulping
covers: Thermomechanical, chemi-thermomechanical and groundwood refining, with refiner heat recovery.
steam: Refiner heat is recovered as low-pressure steam; quantity not in held sources.
draws-on: none (a source: refiner heat is recovered as low-pressure steam)
energy-inputs: electricity (refiners)
note: Split from mechanical-and-recycled-pulping on 2026-09-16: refiners use several times the electricity of repulping and the technologies do not compete. The refiners are the process (rule 5), so they are no longer a link to materials-processing.

label: Recycled-fibre pulping
covers: Recovered-paper repulping, screening, cleaning and deinking.
draws-on: heat-low-temp (repulping and deinking); pumps (stock)
energy-inputs: electricity, steam, deinking chemicals
note: Split from mechanical-and-recycled-pulping on 2026-09-16.

label: Black liquor evaporation and recovery
covers: Multiple-effect evaporators and the recovery furnace.
steam: Evaporators draw steam at up to 110 degC. The recovery furnace is itself a large steam source feeding the heat end uses; its steam conditions are not in held sources.
draws-on: integral (recovery furnace); heat-low-temp (evaporators); fans-and-blowers (combustion air and precipitator)
energy-inputs: black liquor; steam
note: boiler_black-liquor_recovery sits on .steam in design doc s4.1; here it is the chemical-recovery service, with its steam output credited to the heat end uses.

label: Lime kiln
covers: Recausticizing lime kiln.
draws-on: integral (kiln); fans-and-blowers (combustion air)
energy-inputs: natural gas, oil; biomass gasification, tall oil and pitch as alternatives
note: NRCan: 22.6 PJ natural gas and oil at > 700 degC, the mill's main direct fossil heat.

label: Stock preparation, forming and pressing
covers: Stock preparation and refining, headbox and wire, press section, and sheet finishing for all grades.
draws-on: heat-low-temp (stock heating); pumps (stock and white water); compressed-air (showers and doctoring)
energy-inputs: electricity (refiners, vacuum pumps, drives), steam
note: Electricity-dominated; the dryer section is a separate end use.

label: Paper and pulp drying
covers: Dryer section (steam cans, hoods, infrared), coating dryers and market-pulp drying.
service-unit: t water evaporated or t product
heat-process-temp: drying 70-150 [rtc_2023_001 p.88]; drying by steam 38-116 [NREL97 SIC 26xx]; direct-fired dryers 200-700 [nrcan_2025_001]
steam: Dryer-section LP steam -> heat-low-temp. Pulp and paper steam-served heat 81% < 150 degC, 19% at 150-400 [NREL118]; boilers raise 127-149 degC [NREL97].
draws-on: heat-low-temp (steam dryer cans); integral (gas-fired dryers and hoods); fans-and-blowers (hood supply and exhaust)
energy-inputs: steam, natural gas (hoods, IR, air dryers), electricity
note: NRCan: dryers 7.5 PJ at 200-700 degC. CIMS paper grades stay as process steps.

label: Effluent treatment
covers: Primary clarification, biological treatment and sludge handling on mill effluent: aeration basins, activated sludge, anaerobic reactors, clarifiers, presses and dryers.
steam: Anaerobic reactors are held warm; aerobic treatment is unheated.
draws-on: fans-and-blowers (aeration blowers); pumps (effluent and sludge); heat-low-temp (anaerobic reactor heating)
energy-inputs: electricity (aeration blowers, pumps, presses); low-temperature heat (anaerobic reactors); biogas recovered
note: Added 2026-09-15. Aeration is one of the largest single electricity loads in a kraft mill after the refiners and the paper machine, and anaerobic treatment turns part of the load into recovered biogas, so it is a real technology choice rather than generic pumping.

label: Extraction and haulage
covers: Drilling, blasting, loading, hauling and hoisting in open-pit and underground metal, coal and potash mines; solution-mining extraction.
draws-on: none
energy-inputs: diesel (haul trucks, loaders, drills), electricity (hoists, trolley assist, battery equipment)
note: NRCan diesel in mining equipment, trucks and trains: iron ore 7.6 PJ, gold and silver 17.1 PJ.

label: Crushing and grinding
covers: Primary and secondary crushing, milling and grinding, crush-and-screen.
draws-on: materials-processing (mill drives); materials-handling (feed conveying); pumps (mill and cyclone slurry)
energy-inputs: electricity
note: The largest electricity use in metal mining; kept out of machine drive because ore hardness and grind size, not motor choice, set the energy.

label: Mineral separation and processing
covers: Flotation and other separation, cleaning and washing, potash dissolution and crystallization, compaction, tailings disposal.
steam: CIMS Mining.Steam serves potash processing; its temperature is not in held sources.
draws-on: heat-low-temp (potash crystallization and dissolution); pumps (slurry and tailings); fans-and-blowers (flotation blowers)
energy-inputs: electricity (pumps, flotation cells), steam, natural gas

label: Concentrate and product drying
covers: Potash and concentrate drying, and thermal drying of washed coal.
draws-on: integral (direct-fired dryers); fans-and-blowers (dryer air)
energy-inputs: natural gas, coal, electricity
note: Tier is a placeholder until a source gives dryer temperatures.

label: Iron ore pelletizing
covers: Pellet induration at the mine.
steam: None; iron-ore sites run small boilers below 200 degC [nrcan_2025_001].
draws-on: integral (induration furnace); fans-and-blowers (induration and cooler fans)
energy-inputs: heavy oil, natural gas; coke and coal as additives; electricity
note: NRCan: 23.4 PJ in pelletizing furnaces (13.7 PJ oil at > 700 degC). Same technologies as iron-and-steel agglomeration.

label: Mine ventilation and air heating
covers: Underground ventilation fans, mine air heating (and cooling in deep mines).
heat-process-temp: mine air heating, near ambient; no held source gives a figure
draws-on: integral (direct-fired mine air heaters)
energy-inputs: electricity (fans), natural gas and propane (air heaters)
note: Taken out of facility services because of its scale and distinct technologies. NRCan: gold and silver mine space heating 3.8 PJ below 200 degC. CIMS keeps the fan technologies in the shared machine-drive fan service; only the coal mine-air duty (`coal-mining.product.raw-product.mine-ventilation`) is a node of its own, and metal mining has none.

label: Water and tailings management
covers: Mine dewatering, water treatment before discharge or reuse, process-water reclaim, and tailings transport, thickening and storage.
draws-on: pumps (dewatering, reclaim and tailings); fans-and-blowers (aeration)
energy-inputs: electricity (dewatering and reclaim pumps, thickeners, treatment plant); natural gas (evaporative concentration)
note: Added 2026-09-15. Separated from comminution and separation because the driver is the site water balance and the discharge permit, not the ore throughput, and because dewatering pumping runs whether or not the mill does.

label: Drilling and well services
covers: Drilling rigs, completions and hydraulic fracturing, well testing and servicing.
service-unit: m drilled; well tests t CH4; completion GJ hydraulic work
draws-on: field-engines (well-site engines)
energy-inputs: diesel, natural gas (dual-fuel and gas engines), electricity (grid-powered rigs)
note: Fracturing pump spreads are among the largest diesel loads in the sector; electric fleets compete.

label: Conventional oil and gas production
covers: Light, medium, heavy and offshore oil and conventional, tight, shale and coalbed-methane gas wells: artificial lift, field compression, heater-treaters and line heaters, wellsite dehydration, pneumatic controllers and pumps, liquids unloading, enhanced oil recovery.
heat-process-temp: heater-treaters and line heaters; not in held or checked sources
draws-on: heat-low-temp (heater-treaters and line heaters); compressor-drive-engine (field gathering compression); compressor-drive-turbine (field gathering compression); field-engines (well-site engines); integral (artificial lift)
energy-inputs: natural gas (fuel gas, gas-driven pneumatics), electricity, diesel
note: Gas-driven pneumatics are a methane-venting service more than an energy one; CIMS models electric replacements. Field compression is a demand here; the drivers that meet it are compressor-drive-engine and compressor-drive-turbine.

label: Produced water handling
covers: Separation, treatment, recycling and disposal of produced and flowback water: disposal-well injection, de-oiling and softening for steam generation, evaporators and crystallizers, and recycling for makeup.
steam: Evaporators take low-pressure steam or fired heat.
draws-on: pumps (disposal and recycle injection); heat-low-temp (softening and evaporation); integral (fired evaporators)
energy-inputs: electricity (injection and transfer pumps, treatment); natural gas (evaporators, heaters)
note: Added 2026-09-15. In-situ bitumen recycles most of its produced water, so the water plant is part of what sets the steam-to-oil ratio; disposal injection carries its own energy and its own regulatory constraint. Kept out of in-situ-bitumen because it also serves conventional production and fracturing.

label: Venting
covers: Gas deliberately released to atmosphere, and the equipment that avoids, recovers or destroys it: pneumatic controllers and pumps, process and tank venting, blowdowns for maintenance, liquids unloading.
draws-on: compressed-air (vapour recovery and instrument air)
energy-inputs: natural gas (the gas vented, and pneumatic supply gas); electricity (vapour recovery, instrument air)
note: Split from venting-and-flaring on 2026-09-16: other source data report venting and flaring separately, and the CIMS hierarchy keeps them apart. Deliberate release: the volume is event- and equipment-driven and largely metered or estimated per event, and the abatement is equipment substitution. The enclosed combustor destroys vapours that would otherwise be vented, so release and destruction compete here. The service is really tonnes of methane; the unit is the gas disposed of on an energy basis.

label: Flaring
covers: Solution-gas and process flaring: gas burned rather than sold, and the equipment that recovers it or raises destruction efficiency.
draws-on: integral (flare pilots and purge gas); compressed-air (flare gas recovery)
energy-inputs: natural gas (the gas flared, plus pilot and purge gas); electricity (flare gas recovery)
note: Split from venting-and-flaring on 2026-09-16. The service is the gas burned, on an energy basis.

label: Fugitive emissions
covers: Unintentional leaks from valves, flanges, connectors, seals, compressor packings and storage, and the survey, monitoring and component programs that find and cut them.
draws-on: none
energy-inputs: natural gas (the gas leaked); electricity (survey and monitoring equipment)
note: Split from venting and flaring, 2026-09-15. Leaks scale with component count and stock age rather than with throughput, the volume is inferred from emission factors or top-down measurement rather than metered, and the abatement is a program - survey frequency, monitoring, low-emission components - not a device that competes with a vapour recovery unit. Canadian methane regulations set LDAR frequency separately from venting limits. Top-down measurement often cannot attribute observed methane between unburnt flare gas, venting and leaks; where a source does not attribute it, say so rather than splitting on an assumption.

label: In-situ bitumen recovery
covers: SAGD, cyclic steam stimulation, solvent-assisted and hybrid thermal-solvent recovery: steam generation and injection, produced-water treatment and recycling, bitumen treating.
heat-process-temp: saturated steam at reservoir injection pressure; no held or checked source gives the temperature
steam: The dominant use: lifecycle steam-to-oil ratio about 3.5 for SAGD and about 6.0 for CSS (Oil Sands Magazine).
draws-on: heat-medium-temp (once-through field boilers and cogeneration); pumps (injection and produced fluids); produced-water-handling (makeup and recycle); field-engines (site engines)
energy-inputs: natural gas (steam generation), electricity; solvents; produced gas
note: The boilers are separable, so the steam draws on the heat bands. Solvent routes compete by cutting the steam needed rather than supplying it differently. CIMS already offers electric, hydrogen and nuclear steam here.

label: Oil sands mining and extraction
covers: Truck-and-shovel mining, ore preparation and hydrotransport, hot- or warm-water bitumen extraction, froth treatment, tailings handling.
heat-process-temp: Clark hot-water process 80-85 (historical, Alberta Energy Heritage); modern plants run cooler, not quantified in checked sources
steam: Hot process water and some steam for extraction and froth treatment.
draws-on: heat-low-temp (process water heating); pumps (hydrotransport and tailings); materials-handling (ore conveying)
energy-inputs: diesel (haul trucks, shovels), natural gas, electricity
note: The haul fleet stays here rather than in mobile-equipment, as mine haulage does in mining.

label: Bitumen upgrading
covers: Upgraders that turn bitumen into synthetic crude: coking, hydrocracking, hydrotreating, sulphur recovery.
heat-process-temp: as petroleum-refining conversion (reactors ~260-480, rtc_2023_001 p.97); not upgrader-specific
steam: Stripping and process steam, as in refining.
draws-on: heat-medium-temp (fired heaters); heat-high-temp (fired heaters); upgrader-hydrogen (hydroconversion); field-engines (upgrader engines)
energy-inputs: natural gas, still gas and coke, hydrogen, electricity
note: Same technologies as petroleum-refining conversion-and-treating. It is kept in this sector because upgraders are integrated with oil sands operations and CIMS models them in Petroleum Crude.

label: On-site hydrogen production
covers: Hydrogen made at a bitumen upgrader for hydroconversion: steam methane reformers with and without capture, and gasification of asphaltenes or petroleum coke.
steam: Reformer convection sections raise HP steam.
draws-on: integral (reformer firebox); compressed-air (make-up compression)
energy-inputs: natural gas, petroleum coke, electricity
note: Moved out of the cross-sector hydrogen-and-fuel-supply end use (2026-09-14). Quest captures from these reformers, which is why the concentrated-stream capture row sits here.

label: Natural gas processing
covers: Sweetening (amine), dehydration (glycol), sulphur recovery, NGL extraction and fractionation, inlet and sales compression.
heat-process-temp: amine and glycol regeneration; not in held or checked sources
steam: Reboiler steam or direct-fired reboilers for solvent and glycol regeneration.
draws-on: heat-low-temp (reboilers); heat-medium-temp (reboilers); compressor-drive-engine (inlet and sales compression); compressor-drive-turbine (inlet and sales compression); integral (plant refrigeration)
energy-inputs: natural gas, electricity
note: Acid gas stripped from raw gas is concentrated CO2, the classic low-cost capture stream.

label: LNG liquefaction
covers: Gas pre-treatment, refrigeration-cycle compression and liquefaction, boil-off handling.
draws-on: heat-low-temp (amine pre-treatment); integral (refrigerant compression)
energy-inputs: natural gas (gas-turbine compressor drives) or electricity (electric-drive trains)
note: LNG Canada (Kitimat, two trains, 14 Mtpa) shipped its first cargo in 2025 (Shell). The drive choice, gas turbine or electric, is the main technology decision.

label: Natural gas transmission and distribution
covers: Transmission pipelines, with the compression their stations draw from the compressor-drive end uses; pressure let-down stations with their line heaters.
service-unit: 1000 m3 of gas (transported 1000 km, or let down)
draws-on: compressor-drive-engine (compressor stations); compressor-drive-turbine (compressor stations)
energy-inputs: natural gas drawn from the pipeline (turbine and engine compressor drives), electricity (electric-drive compressors), waste-heat recovery
note: Pipeline transport emitted 8.3 Mt CO2e in 2019, mostly from compressor-station combustion (CER). Transmission and distribution leaks add 2.4 Mt, but those are emissions, not energy. The compression is a demand here; the drivers that meet it are compressor-drive-engine and compressor-drive-turbine, split by driver as the CIMS hierarchy splits them (2026-09-22). Product 1000 m3, the CIMS transmission basis: pipeline_natural-gas per 1000 m3 moved 1000 km (pipe only), and the let-down valve and turboexpander per 1000 m3 let down (Brad 2026-10-29).

label: Field engines
covers: Stationary diesel, gasoline and propane engines at oil and gas sites, driving pumps, generators and other field equipment: requested per well, per m3 of bitumen and by upgraders. Excludes compressor drivers and haul fleets, which have their own end uses.
draws-on: none
energy-inputs: diesel, gasoline, propane; electricity (motor replacement)
note: One end use for the one CIMS node, crude-oil.service.field-engines (2026-09-22). Drilling, production, in-situ bitumen and upgrading reference it through draws-on instead of each claiming part of it.

label: Compressor drive, reciprocating
covers: Reciprocating compressors and their drivers, mostly natural gas engines, with electric-motor replacements, meeting field gathering, gas-processing and pipeline compression demand.
draws-on: none
energy-inputs: natural gas (fuel gas); electricity (electric-motor drive)
note: Split by driver as the CIMS hierarchy does, natural-gas.service.compressor-drive.engine (CIMS Direct Drive Small, 10-year life, 2026-09-22). The three compression end uses draw on it in exogenous shares. Rod packing and blowdowns are methane sources counted on venting and fugitive-emissions.

label: Compressor drive, gas turbine
covers: Centrifugal compressors and their drivers, mostly natural gas turbines, with large electric-motor replacements, meeting processing and pipeline compression demand and some field compression.
draws-on: none
energy-inputs: natural gas (fuel gas); electricity (electric-motor drive); recovered exhaust heat
note: Split by driver as the CIMS hierarchy does, natural-gas.service.compressor-drive.turbine (CIMS Direct Drive Large, 30-year life, 2026-09-22). Turbine exhaust is the waste-heat-to-power opportunity at compressor stations.

label: Crude oil and liquids pipelines
covers: Crude, bitumen-blend, and refined-product trunk pipelines, with the pumping their stations draw from crude-pipeline-pumping.
draws-on: crude-pipeline-pumping (pump stations)
note: Oil pipelines mostly use electric motors, so they emit much less than gas pipelines (CER). Pipe only (Brad 2026-10-29), as the gas pipeline: the pump stations are their own pumping node, crude-pipeline-pumping.

label: Crude pipeline pumping
covers: Pump stations on crude, bitumen-blend, and refined-product pipelines, with drag-reducing agents and heating where used.
service-unit: m3 pumped 1000 km (m3-km in the long tables)
draws-on: none
energy-inputs: electricity (pump motors); some engine-driven pumps
note: Node added 2026-10-29 at the modeller's request, ahead of CIMS (Brad 2026-10-29): the crude pipeline requests pumping as the gas pipeline requests compression. Oil pipelines mostly use electric motors, so they emit much less than gas pipelines (CER).

label: Cooking, pasteurizing and sterilizing
covers: Cooking, blanching, scalding, pasteurizing, sterilizing and retorting, evaporating and concentrating, brewing, washing and CIP.
heat-process-temp: pasteurizing 60-140, sterilizing 110-120, washing 60-90, cooking 95-200 [rtc_2023_001 p.66]; pasteurization 73, retort 100-121, evaporating 52-121 [NREL97 SIC 2026, 2033, 2046, 2075]
steam: Steam and hot water. Boilers raise 121-177 degC steam [NREL97 SIC 20xx]; 99% of steam-served heat is below 150 degC [NREL118].
draws-on: heat-low-temp (cooking, pasteurizing and clean-in-place); pumps (product transfer); compressed-air (packaging and controls)
energy-inputs: natural gas, electricity, biomass

label: Baking, frying and roasting
covers: Ovens, fryers and roasters.
heat-process-temp: baking 100-232 [NREL97 SIC 2051, 2052]; roasting 93 [SIC 2046]; cooking up to 200 [rtc_2023_001 p.66]
steam: Minor: proofing steam at 38 degC [NREL97 SIC 2051].
draws-on: integral (ovens, fryers and roasters); fans-and-blowers (oven air and exhaust)
energy-inputs: natural gas, electricity
note: Harmonized files ovens under process-heat-high-temp; the sources put them at 100-232 degC.

label: Drying and curing
covers: Spray, drum, belt and grain drying; sugar and pulp drying.
heat-process-temp: drying 30-90 [rtc_2023_001 p.66]; drying 38-121 [NREL97 SIC 20xx]; sugar calcining 316 [SIC 2063]
draws-on: integral (direct-fired dryers); heat-low-temp (steam dryers); fans-and-blowers (dryer air)
energy-inputs: natural gas, steam, electricity (heat pump and MVR dryers)

label: Refrigeration and cold storage
covers: Chilling, freezing and cold storage: vapour-compression plant, ammonia and CO2 systems, spiral and blast freezers, and the cold rooms they serve.
steam: None. Absorption machines take low-temperature heat.
draws-on: heat-low-temp (absorption machines)
energy-inputs: electricity; low-temperature heat (absorption machines)
note: Moved out of the cross-sector process-cooling-and-refrigeration end use (2026-09-14): food and beverage is where process cooling is a real energy service. Chemical-plant and gas-plant refrigeration stays inside the process end use it serves.

label: Alumina digestion
covers: Bayer digestion, clarification, precipitation and liquor evaporation (everything but calcination).
steam: Digestion steam at 146 degC [NREL97], at the low/medium boundary; alumina boilers < 200 degC [nrcan_2025_001].
draws-on: heat-low-temp (digestion steam); pumps (slurry and liquor)
energy-inputs: natural gas, electricity
note: NRCan: boiler 3.0 PJ. Split from alumina-refining 2026-10-28 (Brad).

label: Alumina calcination
covers: Calcination of alumina hydrate to alumina.
draws-on: integral (calciner)
energy-inputs: natural gas, electricity
note: NRCan: calciner 4.5 PJ. Split from alumina-refining 2026-10-28 (Brad).

label: Aluminum smelting
covers: Hall-Heroult electrolysis (prebake and Soderberg cells); inert-anode cells.
draws-on: integral (resistive cell heat); fans-and-blowers (pot gas and dry scrubbing)
energy-inputs: electricity; carbon anodes consumed
note: NRCan: 45.0 PJ petroleum coke consumed as anode carbon (non-energetic).

label: Anode production
covers: Prebake anode baking and Soderberg paste.
draws-on: integral (baking furnace)
energy-inputs: natural gas, oil; pitch and coke as feed
note: NRCan: 5.4 PJ.

label: Fuel-fired roasting, smelting and refining
covers: Roasting, flash, continuous and conventional smelting, converting and fire refining for copper, nickel, lead and zinc, and the silicothermic retort for magnesium.
draws-on: integral (smelting and converting); smelter-oxygen-supply (enrichment); smelter-acid-plant (SO2 off-gas, 2.5-4.0 t acid per t copper); fans-and-blowers (off-gas handling)
energy-inputs: natural gas, coke, coal, electricity, oxygen

label: Oxygen supply
covers: Cryogenic and adsorption air separation supplying oxygen enrichment to flash and bath smelting and to converting.
draws-on: none (the air compressors are the process)
energy-inputs: electricity (compression)
note: Moved out of the cross-sector air-separation end use (2026-09-14). Oxygen enrichment is what sets smelter fuel use, so it belongs with the smelter.

label: Smelter acid plant
covers: Gas cleaning and contact (double absorption) sulphuric acid plants that capture the SO2 in smelting and converting off-gas; the service is t of sulphuric acid made.
steam: Exports some steam from the converter and absorption heat (HRS); not counted.
draws-on: none (the main blowers are the process)
energy-inputs: electricity (main blowers, gas cleaning)
note: Added 2026-10-27 ahead of CIMS (S95, Brad): the acid plant is about 30% of a copper smelter's capex (Schlesinger 2011 Table 22.6) and no other node carries it. Smelting and converting request about 2.5-4.0 t acid per t copper (Schlesinger 2011 Ch. 12, depending on the S/Cu ratio of the feed).

label: Electric smelting (silicon, ferroalloys, titanium slag)
covers: Submerged-arc and electric smelting furnaces for silicon metal, ferrosilicon and other ferroalloys, and titanium slag from ilmenite.
heat-process-temp: heating 816, drying 204 [NREL97 SIC 3313]; furnace temperatures not in held sources
draws-on: integral (electric furnace)
energy-inputs: electricity (dominant); coal, coke, charcoal and wood chips as reductants
note: Ferroglobe Becancour runs two 24 MW and one 32 MW furnaces for silicon metal and ferrosilicon. Rio Tinto Fer et Titane (Sorel-Tracy) has capacity for about 1.35 Mt/yr of titanium slag. NAICS codes ferroalloys to 331110 (iron and steel); they sit here on the user's decision because the energy use is electric smelting, not steelmaking. Rio Tinto Fer et Titane co-produces about 1 Mt/yr of pig iron; all of the furnace energy and the reductant CO2 stay with the slag and the iron is taken as a co-product carrying none, because one furnace makes both and no allocation basis exists. The pig iron appears on the demand side as foundry feed (other-industry/metal-melting-and-heat-treatment).
sources: NREL97; Ferroglobe Becancour (web); QIT-Fer et Titane (web)

label: Leaching and electrowinning
covers: Leaching, solvent extraction, electrowinning and electrorefining, and molten-salt electrolysis (magnesium cells).
steam: Low-temperature steam at about 60 degC [NREL97]. Non-ferrous steam-served heat is 100% below 150 degC [NREL118].
draws-on: heat-low-temp (electrolyte heating); pumps (leach and electrolyte circulation)
energy-inputs: electricity, steam

label: Melting, casting, rolling and extrusion
covers: Secondary aluminum, melt and cast shops, holding and reheating furnaces, homogenizing, hot and cold rolling, extrusion.
draws-on: integral (melting and holding furnaces); compressed-air (casting and handling)
energy-inputs: natural gas, electricity (induction)
note: NRCan: aluminum reheating furnaces 2.7 PJ. Semi-fabrication is about 20% of US aluminum energy (hot rolling 10.1%, extrusion 5.3%, cold rolling 4.7%; DOE 2017 aluminum bandwidth study). Canada is mostly primary smelting, so it is folded in here rather than given its own end use.
sources: NREL97; nrcan_2025_001; DOE 2017 aluminum bandwidth study (web)

label: Metal melting and heat treatment
covers: Foundry melting, forging, heat treating and annealing in fabricated metals, machinery and transport equipment.
draws-on: integral (melting and heat-treatment furnaces); compressed-air (quenching and handling)
energy-inputs: natural gas, electricity (induction, arc), coke (cupolas)

label: Fuel blending
covers: Nodes that blend a commodity into supply. No technology serves them.
note: not served by the database

label: By-product fuel routing
covers: By-product fuels whose heat is counted on the steam, reheating and direct-heat nodes they feed.
note: not served by the database

label: Light-industry demand nodes
covers: Product nodes that request heat, refrigeration, steam and machine drive; those services carry the energy.
note: not served by the database

label: Agricultural feedstock
covers: Feedstock supply to biofuels.

covers: Coal-to-liquids and gas-to-liquids (Fischer-Tropsch) plants making liquid fuels from coal or natural gas.
note: Node added 2026-10-09 at the modeller's request, ahead of CIMS (hierarchy-change-requests.md).

label: Oil sands tailings
covers: Treatment and disposal of oil sands tailings (dry stacking, centrifuging, thickening).
note: Node added 2026-10-09 at the modeller's request, ahead of CIMS.

label: Petrochemical feedstock
covers: Feedstocks supplied to petrochemical crackers, including recycled-plastic pyrolysis oil.
note: Annotation added 2026-10-09 for reactor_plastics-pyrolysis.

label: N2O abatement
covers: Catalytic or thermal destruction of the N2O from nitric and adipic acid plants, requested by those plants.
note: added 2026-10-22 (node-split review 2026-10-22 (database/reviews/node-split-review_2026-10-22.csv))

label: Distillation
covers: Distillation trains separating petrochemical intermediates and products, requested by the petrochemical nodes.
note: added 2026-10-22 (node-split review 2026-10-22 (database/reviews/node-split-review_2026-10-22.csv))

label: Cement binders and blending
covers: The cement recipe: each binder requests clinker, grinding and supplementary materials (calcined clay, ground slag) per t cement from their own nodes, and holds only its own blending and handling (S121, Brad 2026-10-27: cement restructured into recipes and supplementary-material nodes).
note: added 2026-10-22 (node-split review 2026-10-22 (database/reviews/node-split-review_2026-10-22.csv))

label: Ground granulated slag
covers: Granulated blast-furnace slag dried and ground to cement fineness (GGBFS), per t of ground slag; the slag itself is a blast-furnace by-product.
note: Added 2026-10-27 (S121, Brad 2026-10-27: cement restructured into recipes and supplementary-material nodes). Slag blends and alkali-activated binders request it.

label: Calcined clay
covers: Clay calcined at 700-900 degC to a pozzolan for LC3 and other blends, per t of calcined clay.
note: Added 2026-10-27 (S121, Brad 2026-10-27: cement restructured into recipes and supplementary-material nodes). LC3 requests about 0.30 t per t cement.

label: Coal-mine methane
covers: Drainage and ventilation-air methane control, requested by coal extraction.
note: added 2026-10-22 (node-split review 2026-10-22 (database/reviews/node-split-review_2026-10-22.csv))

label: Solid biofuels (pellets)
covers: Wood pellets and torrefied pellets.
note: added 2026-10-22 (node-split review 2026-10-22 (database/reviews/node-split-review_2026-10-22.csv))

label: Forming and pressing
covers: Heated presses (panel hot presses).
service-unit: GJ process heat (wood products: t dry fibre)
note: added 2026-10-22 (node-split review 2026-10-22 (database/reviews/node-split-review_2026-10-22.csv))

label: Foundry melting
covers: Iron and steel foundry melting: cupolas, induction, crucible, isothermal and oxy-fuel rotary furnaces, and foundry EAFs.
note: node-split follow-up 2026-10-22: foundry melting split from light-industrial metal melting, so one end use is not shown in two products

label: Aromatics
covers: Benzene, toluene and xylenes recovered from reformate or pyrolysis gasoline by extraction and distillation; in Canada mostly refinery-integrated (Sarnia, Alberta).
note: added (petrochemicals restructure 2026-10-23 (modeller: whatever makes most sense for Canada))

label: Polymers
covers: Polyethylene and polypropylene reactors with extrusion and pelletizing (Alberta and Sarnia).
note: added (petrochemicals restructure 2026-10-23 (modeller: whatever makes most sense for Canada))

label: Olefin derivatives
covers: Ethylene oxide and glycol (Alberta) and other olefin and aromatic derivatives, and chemical depolymerization back to monomers.
note: added (petrochemicals restructure 2026-10-23 (modeller: whatever makes most sense for Canada))

label: Ammonia
covers: Ammonia synthesis: steam or autothermal reforming, coal or biomass gasification, or electrolytic hydrogen, with the Haber-Bosch loop.
note: added (naming and end-use split 2026-10-23 (modeller))

label: Methanol
covers: Methanol synthesis from reformed natural gas, gasified coal or biomass, or captured CO2 and hydrogen.
note: added (naming and end-use split 2026-10-23 (modeller))

label: Hydrogen peroxide
covers: Anthraquinone autoxidation plants (pulp bleaching supply).
note: added (naming and end-use split 2026-10-23 (modeller))

label: Urea
covers: Urea synthesis from ammonia and the ammonia plant's CO2.
note: added (naming and end-use split 2026-10-23 (modeller))

label: Other fertilizers
covers: Ammonium nitrate and calcium ammonium nitrate, UAN, and ammonium phosphates and sulphate.
note: added (naming and end-use split 2026-10-23 (modeller))

label: Oxygen supply
covers: Cryogenic and adsorption air separation supplying oxygen to oxy-fuel glass furnaces, on site or over the fence (node added 2026-11-05).
draws-on: none (the air compressors are the process)
energy-inputs: electricity (compression)
note: Added with the node alignment review (IM11, Brad 2026-11-05): oxy-fuel glass furnaces buy oxygen per t melt. Oxy-fuel and calcium-looping cement and lime kilns keep their air separation unit on the kiln.
